purpose: RSA-PSS SigVer KAT, tests PKCS#11 CKM_SHA256_RSA_PKCS_PSS (C_VerifyInit/C_Verify). Vectors are sourced from ACVP's sigGen test type (n, e, message, signature), not sigVer: sigGen groups carry no testPassed field because every case is, by construction, a correct signature produced by NIST's own reference generator, so they are directly usable as positive sigVer material (the same repurposing rsa_oaep_test.json's note documents for KTS-IFC decrypt-direction data). testPassed is set explicitly here for harness clarity.

_provenance.note: WS-0.5 continuation: an earlier session (commit c54ea27, 'ACVP test-vector resync + provenance backfill (#186)') concluded 'NIST's reference PSS vectors use hash families neither engine's PSS path implements at all' and left rsapss_test.json with zero _provenance, self-generated content only. Re-investigated from scratch per WS-0.4 instructions rather than trusting that note, and it does not hold: it is true of the RSA-SigVer-FIPS186-5 sample specifically (its 45 groups are all SHAKE-128/SHAKE-256/SHA3-256 combinations under FIPS 186-5's PSS-with-SHAKE scheme, which neither engine implements - C++'s OSSLRSA.cpp PSS switch has no SHAKE case, and even its SHA3-256 case requires MGF1-SHA3-256, not the shake-128/shake-256 mask functions this sample uses; Rust's handlers.rs has no CKM_SHA3_256_RSA_PKCS_PSS arm at all) - but it is false of RSA-SigGen-FIPS186-5 and RSA-SigGen-FIPS186-4, whose sample sets both include a plain SHA2-256, MGF1(SHA2-256) PSS group (this file's tgId 9, and FIPS186-4's tgId 13), which is exactly CKM_SHA256_RSA_PKCS_PSS - implemented in BOTH engines: C++ OSSLRSA.cpp:335-355 (RSA_SHA256_PKCS_PSS, MGF1_SHA256 required) and Rust handlers.rs:2333 (CKM_SHA256_RSA_PKCS_PSS, sha2::Sha256). The only unusual thing about this group is saltLen=8 (NIST's sample deliberately does not use the conventional digest-length salt); this is NOT a compatibility problem for either engine - C++'s sLen check (OSSLRSA.cpp:346, 'sLen > modBytes-2-hashLen') is an UPPER bound only, and Rust's verify_rsa (handlers.rs:2313-2314, pss_salt_len Some(s) => vec![s]) uses the caller-supplied sLen verbatim as the sole verification candidate - so an 8-byte salt round-trips correctly through CK_RSA_PKCS_PSS_PARAMS.sLen on both. tgId 9, tcId 25/26/27 (2048-bit modulus, all three tests in the group) selected. Cross-checked independently with Python's `cryptography` library (RSA public-key PSS verify, SHA-256, MGF1-SHA256, salt_length=8) before writing - 3/3 VALID. tests/helpers.mjs's rsaVerify() previously hardcoded sLen=32 (matching the old self-generated vector, which invented a conventional digest-length salt) and took a text message via TextEncoder; both were real vectors this fix could not have passed against, so rsaVerify() was changed to take raw message bytes and an explicit sLen override, and acvp-wasm.mjs's RSA-PSS KAT updated to pass tv.message (hex) and testGroups[0].saltLen. WS-5.1 (2026-08-30): extended from 1 testGroup to 9 — added tgId 100-107 covering pkcs1v1.5 {SHA-1,SHA2-224,SHA2-256,SHA2-512,SHA3-512} and pss {SHA-1,SHA2-224,SHA3-256}, going from 1 of 22 advertised RSA signature mechanisms with real evidence to 9. Sourced from 4 different ACVP-Server RSA sigGen/sigVer revisions (see _provenance_multi) because no single sample dataset at this pinned commit covers more than 2-3 hash algorithms — this appears to be an inherent characteristic of the curated sample vector sets NIST publishes, not a gap in what was fetched. SHA-384 and SHA3-224/384 remain uncovered: not present in any of the 4 revisions checked (RSA-SigGen-FIPS186-4/5, RSA-SigVer-FIPS186-2/4/5).
